extracted.intended_audience: San Francisco city officials, appointed board and commission members, department staff, and other public-sector actors seeking guidance on ethics, open-government, and meeting/records laws
extracted.subtask_description: Practical legal and policy standards governing the conduct of San Francisco public officials, members of boards and commissions, and related City employees — covering appointments, conflicts of interest, financial disclosure, gifts, public meetings, and public records requests. The guide explains duties, prohibitions, procedures, and enforcement mechanisms specific to City and overlapping state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of boards and commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing how boards and commissions are created under City law (charter/ordinance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of powers, duties, restrictions relating to commissions; role of Board of Supervisors and delegations; procedural requirements for establishing bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: The appointment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements and criteria for becoming a commissioner, including appointing authority responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains steps in appointment, expectations of appointees, interaction with mayoral/Board offices, and reference to residency and other eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency and other requirements for commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility rules (such as residency) that must be met to serve on particular boards or commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies where residency is required and notes other statutory or charter eligibility constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of office
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that commissioners take an oath of office before performing official duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides timing and form of oath and legal significance for service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and benefits for commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on commissioner compensation, term and tenure, health benefits, and reimbursement of expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes nominal pay vs. benefits; addresses reimbursement procedures and allowable expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners are officers of the City
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal status of commissioners as City officers with attendant duties and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains implications for ethics, conflicts rules, and public records obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance expectations and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for commissioner attendance, including the Mayor’s baseline standards (excused absences, working goal of 100% attendance, practical 90% target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires commission secretaries to report attendance annually; asks liaison contact when commissioner misses without notice or misses three meetings in a fiscal year; encourages internal attendance policies per Board resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of commissioners at meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral standards and prohibitions on discriminatory or harassing remarks at public meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair must read City’s policy if discriminatory/harassing remarks occur, excuse offended City employees, may recess the meeting, and follow Brown Act procedures for willful disruption (Sheriff assistance, clearing room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of commissioners and commission officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined roles (members, officers, secretary) including powers, duties, election of officers, and restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains officer functions, election procedures, quorum and voting rules, and duties of commission secretaries and department heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial disclosure (Statements of Economic Interests - SEIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who must file SEIs, what must be disclosed, where and when to file, and consequences for failure to file or disclose required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules on amendments, public access, Sunshine affidavit for certain filers, and links to Ethics Commission forms and regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest test — reasonably foreseeable financial effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Political Reform Act inquiry: 'Is it reasonably foreseeable that the governmental decision will have a financial effect on any of the public official’s financial interests?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides officials to analyze foreseeability before assessing materiality or disqualification requirements; used as first step in conflict analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest test — materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Political Reform Act: 'Will the reasonably foreseeable financial effect be material?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific sub-analyses for types of interests: business entities, real property, sources of income, sources of gifts, and personal finances; each category has distinct materiality thresholds/explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest test — distinguishable effect from public generally
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether any material financial effect on the official’s interest is distinguishable from its effect on the public generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not distinguishable, the official may not have a disqualifying conflict under the PRA; guidance includes tests and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation/use of position to influence a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the public official is making, participating in making, or attempting to use official position to influence a governmental decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If so, combined with a disqualifying economic interest, the official must disqualify; includes an exception for legally required participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions involving a financial interest in a business entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for materiality and disqualification where the official has a financial interest in a business entity affected by the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on types of business interests, valuation thresholds, and examples of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions involving a financial interest in real property
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules analyzing foreseeability and materiality for decisions affecting real property in which the official has an interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on proximity, zoning changes, and other property-specific factors that can create disqualifying conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions involving a financial interest in a source of income
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis for conflicts where an official’s source of income may be affected by the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies lookback periods, amount thresholds, and when income sources trigger disqualification under PRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions involving a financial interest in a source of gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict analysis for decisions affecting a source of gifts to the official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when gifts or gift sources create disqualifying interests and addresses reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions involving a financial interest in personal finances
rubrics_metrics.description: Materiality analysis for decisions that affect an official’s personal finances outside of business/entity/property/income categorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples and tests for personal financial impacts giving rise to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: legally required participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited circumstances where an official’s participation is legally required despite potential conflict (statutory or constitutional obligations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains narrow scope and how to determine applicability; officials should consult counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts under Government Code section 1090 (contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on officials being financially interested in contracts made by them or by the agency (Gov. Code § 1090 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who is subject, what constitutes a 'financial interest' and a 'making a contract', and addresses remote/noninterests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts under common law, local Campaign & Governmental Conduct Code, and bribery/misuse of office
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader prohibitions on conflicts of interest including common law duties, local code provisions, bribery, and misuse of office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes overlap with statutory conflicts and additional potential civil/criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recusal and disqualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When board members and commissioners must recuse themselves if they have conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural steps for announcing recusal and documenting it in the record; ties to PRA, Gov. Code 1090, and local rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on representing private parties before City officers (compensated advocacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ban on representing or advocating on behalf of private parties for compensation before City officers/employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses scope, exceptions, and enforcement; applies to currently serving officers and sometimes former employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on future employment and revolving-door rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-employment restrictions: permanent bans and one-year restriction on communications for former employees/officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details different restrictions for all officers/employees, special rules for former Mayors and Supervisors, waiver rules, and how restrictions apply to communications and contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on incompatible activities and holding more than one office
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules prohibiting activities or dual offices that are incompatible with City duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes process for statements of incompatible activities and advance written determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contracting with the City
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions preventing officers from entering into contracts with the City under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory bases, exceptions, and how conflicts are assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disclosing or using confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions forbidding officers/employees from using or disclosing confidential City information for private gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what information is confidential and disciplinary/enforcement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on the use of City resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules limiting use of City staff, facilities, funds or materials for non-City or political purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains permissible uses vs. prohibited political/fundraising activities and penalties for misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on political activity and fundraising by City officers/employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on soliciting campaign contributions, volunteers, and other political activities while using City position or resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes contractor contribution ban, bans on solicitation/receipt from contractors, and rules for board members running for elective office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor contribution bans and restrictions related to land-use matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibitions on contributions by contractors and by persons with pending land use matters to elected officials or candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when bans apply and related disqualification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts — general rule and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework defining 'gift', rules on recipient disqualification, and analysis framework for gift-related conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes local 'restricted source' rule, state gift limits, reporting requirements, and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local 'restricted source' gift rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Local rule defining restricted sources and when gifts from those sources are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines restricted source, describes prohibited circumstances, exceptions, and other local gift restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State gift limits and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: California Political Reform Act limits on gifts and related reporting obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes exceptions, categories of reportable-but-not-limited gifts, and interaction with local rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for honoraria, travel, and loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific restrictions and disclosure requirements governing honoraria, travel reimbursements, and loans received by officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details examples, allowable exceptions, and how travel or loans are reported or treated as gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts to the City and departmental acceptance/reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules allowing departments to accept gifts (up to $10,000) and requiring departments to report all gifts and handling gifts that benefit particular employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains reporting, distribution of gifts by the City, and ticket/event pass rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behested payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and reporting rules for payments made at the behest of City officials (behested payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both City officers/employees filing SEIs and elected officials; explains reporting timelines and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interested parties and exceptions under nonprofit contracting ordinance
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of 'interested parties' and exceptions for nonprofit entities subject to certain disclosure/board composition rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes community representation requirement on boards, notice of vacancies, public comment at designated meetings, and how to comply by mailing records for sensitive services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement process for nonprofit ordinance noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-stage non-binding dispute resolution: contracting department review and recommended resolution; optional Sunshine Ordinance Task Force advisory review; Board of Supervisors review and recommended resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes, but does not require, contracting departments to terminate or decline to renew contracts for material breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of passive meeting body rules to private entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances where Sunshine Ordinance passive meeting body rules apply to private entities (e.g., private adviser bodies to policy bodies, social gatherings where a majority invited, private entities managing property with City interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies disclosure obligations, when meetings/records must be made available, and the obligation to provide time/place/nature of events upon inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Brown Act and Public Records Act to certain private entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrow situations where the Brown Act and PRA apply to private boards: where created by Board of Supervisors to exercise delegated authority, or where entity receives City funds and includes an appointed voting member of a City policy body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these cases the entity must conduct meetings under the Brown Act and its records are public records under the PRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum, voting, and meeting operations rules (Brown Act and local rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing quorum, voting, notice, election of officers, order of business, and meeting procedures for City boards and commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural limits on Board of Supervisors communications with departments, exceptions (resolutions, testimony, budget, legislation), and rules on non-interference with administrative matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Supervisors non-interference rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter section 2.114 prohibition against the Board interfering with administration; limits on communications and role in administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains general rule, exceptions (e.g., power of inquiry), and permitted actions like adopting resolutions, budget adoption, testifying, and adopting legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public records definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of a public record: a 'writing' containing information relating to the conduct of the public’s business, prepared, owned, used, or retained by a state or local agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists what qualifies as a writing, who/what is an agency, and describes exceptions to the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public records request formality and identifiability
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for public records requests: form of request, requirement that records sought be 'identifiable', no standing requests, and that questions are not records requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No justification required; anonymous requests permitted; agencies must provide assistance and may ask clarifying questions about identifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely response deadlines for public records requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory response timelines: standard requests — 10 calendar days; immediate disclosure requests — next business day; description requests — 7 calendar days; duties to calculate time, produce records incrementally, and follow the 'rule of reason.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on how to calculate time, incremental production, and agency obligations to search and respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to search and types of responses to records requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must search for responsive records and may respond in various ways (produce, deny under exemption, provide descriptions), with no duty to create new records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No privilege log required; rules on electronic records handling and providing assistance to requesters; agencies must describe records when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for public records requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee rules: no fees for records search, redaction, or inspection; fees permitted for copies (10 cents/page referenced in forms), special fees for copies/services and electronic records; certain exemptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains allowed fees, when fees can be charged, and special fees for extensive copying or electronic retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from disclosure under the Public Records Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated exemptions: privacy interests (employee/public), pending litigation, attorney-client communications, attorney work product, informant identities, trade secrets, investigative and security records, contracts and negotiation strategy, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how exemptions operate, mandatory post-award disclosure rules for contracts, and examples like score sheets/evaluation materials and trade secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures regarding disclosure of contract-related records
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing disclosure of contracts: mandatory post-award disclosure, notice of disclosure requirements, and limited categories (financial data, negotiation strategy, drafts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies redactions and exemptions for sensitive parts of procurement records and when certain materials must remain confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayor’s policy on commissioner attendance (implementation guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mayoral policy expecting excused absences, working goal of 100% attendance (practical 90% target), annual attendance reports to the Mayor’s office, and liaison notifications for unexplained absences or repeated misses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges commissions to incorporate standards into internal policies and notes attendance as a factor in future appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayor’s policy on discriminatory or harassing remarks at public meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: City policy prohibiting discrimination/harassment at public meetings and step-by-step procedures for chairs to address violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair must read policy into the record, excuse offended employees, remind/recess if remarks continue, and treat willful disruptions under Brown Act removal/room-clearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for annual Sunshine, ethics, and sexual harassment training for commissioners and relevant officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies frequency and topics; suggests consulting City Attorney’s Office for advice and training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and penalties for ethics violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties under the Political Reform Act, Government Code section 1090, local codes, and other enforcement mechanisms for violations of ethics laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains civil, administrative, and criminal consequences and enforcement processes, including referral to Ethics Commission or other bodies.
